title: Exact native coefficient inverse image preserves lisse local models
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic absolute-value topology, and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any scheme $X$, let $B_X$ be the sheaf of locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued functions: its sections on $U$ are continuous functions $|U|\to\Omega$ such that every point has an open neighbourhood on which the values span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. Restrictions are by precomposition. This is the coefficient construction used in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], applied to $X$ itself. Write $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$. Call an object lisse if it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $B_U^{\oplus r_U}$ with $r_U$ a finite nonnegative integer, allowed to vary with the covering member $U$. For every morphism of schemes $g:Y\to X$, the canonical coefficient map $g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ induced by precomposition is an isomorphism. The module inverse image $g^*M=B_Y\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X}g^{-1}M$ is exact and sends lisse objects to lisse objects. It sends $B_X^{\oplus r}$ to $B_Y^{\oplus r}$. For $h:Z\to Y$ the canonical inverse-image comparisons identify $h^*g^*$ with $(g\circ h)^*$, and $\operatorname{id}^*$ with the identity.

source.place: Module.lean:120-178 (module inverse image and exactness), Constructible.lean:190-200 (lisse pullback), UpperStar.lean:263-312 (canonical coefficient isomorphism), Module.lean:307-318 (identity and composition comparisons). Bhatt-Scholze, Lemma 4.2.12 and Definition 6.8.1 motivate the coefficient construction; the precise locally finite-functions assertion is the native Lean statement.

proof.text: For $V\to X$ define $\eta_g(t)$ on $V\times_XY$ by $t\circ\operatorname{pr}_V$. Continuity is preserved by precomposition; the inverse image of a neighbourhood on which $t$ has finite-dimensional span has image contained in that same span. Hence this gives a section of $B_Y$. Pointwise addition, multiplication and $1$ commute with precomposition, and the pullback projection identities give compatibility with restrictions. Thus $\eta_g:B_X\to g_*B_Y$ is a ring-sheaf morphism. Take its adjoint $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ for the inverse-image adjunction.

Apply the local generators and relations criterion with $P=u_g:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $F=B_X$, $G=B_Y$, considered as abelian sheaves, and $\eta=\eta_g$. The chosen small sites and larger coefficient universe are those of the inverse-image construction; $u_g$ sends coverings to coverings and preserves the terminal object and fibre products, hence binary products. For a section $s$ and each point of its domain, the local-presentation lemma supplies an affine open on which $s$ is the pullback of a section of $B_X$. These opens cover the domain and give condition (i). For condition (ii), the zero-relation lemma applies to the continuous function underlying $t\in B_X(V)$: its opens cover $U$, its maps $a$ give $B_X(a)t=0$ by pointwise equality, and its factorization identity is exactly the criterion's identity. Thus $c_g$ is an isomorphism on abelian sheaves. Its inverse respects multiplication and the unit, since those identities can be checked after the bijective map $c_g$, so it is the asserted ring-sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Lines 269-312, local generation, local relations and coefficient isomorphism

proof.text: The geometric inverse image with transported $g^{-1}B_X$-action is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by the cited exactness theorem. By the previous step the scalar extension in $g^*M=B_Y\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X}g^{-1}M$ merely transports that action through $c_g$. Explicitly its underlying abelian sheaf is identified with $g^{-1}M$ by $b\otimes m\mapsto c_g^{-1}(b)m$, inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. These formulas respect the balancing relation and are mutually inverse; they define sheaf maps by the sheaf tensor-product construction. Consequently the exact sequences supplied by geometric inverse image remain exact with the transported $B_Y$-actions, proving exactness of $g^*$.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first assertion and proof; native Module.lean:155-178

proof.text: The canonical composition and identity comparisons for the site inverse images are monoidal by the cited theorem. The coefficient maps respect them: the adjunct of the coefficient comparison for $g\circ h$ sends $t$ to its precomposition with the projection to its original domain; precomposing first for $g$, then for $h$, gives this same function under the fibre-product associator. The identity projection gives $t$ itself. The inverse-image adjunction therefore identifies $c_{g\circ h}$ with $c_h\circ h^{-1}(c_g)$ and $c_{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity. The monoidal inverse-image comparisons consequently respect the transported module actions. Together with the explicit scalar-transport identifications of step 3 they give the canonical natural isomorphisms $h^*g^*\cong(g\circ h)^*$ and $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$, with the stated coefficient maps.

source.place: Lines 184-212 and 307-318, coefficient precomposition and module inverse-image comparisons; Stacks sites.tex Tag 00X6, proposition-get-morphism

proof.text: Under scalar transport, $g^*B_X$ identifies with $B_Y$: the map on the scalar-extension presentation is $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,c_g(a)$, inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Exact additive pullback preserves finite biproducts: apply it to the inclusions and projections and to the identities $p_i i_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i i_i p_i=1$. Thus $g^*(B_X^{\oplus r})\cong B_Y^{\oplus r}$. For $r=0$ both sides are zero, since exactness preserves the zero object.

Let $(U_i\to X)$ be a pro-etale covering trivializing a lisse $M$, with ranks $r_i$. Weakly etale base change and fpqc-covering base change show that $(U_i\times_XY\to Y)$ is again a pro-etale covering. Apply the ringed-site pullback/localization comparison to $u_g$ and the object $U_i$. Its hypotheses hold because $u_g$ preserves finite limits and coverings, and so does its slice functor $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/(U_i\times_XY)$; the required left adjoints of the global and slice module pushforwards are the tensor-formula pullbacks $B\otimes_{c^{-1}B}c^{-1}(-)$ along the precomposition coefficient maps, by the ringed-topos module adjunction applied to the geometric morphisms of these site functors. By uniqueness of left adjoints the global one is $g^*$. The weakly-etale localization equivalence identifies these slice sites with the small pro-etale sites of $U_i$ and $U_i\times_XY$; the restricted coefficient rings are literally their locally finite functions. The comparison identifies $(g^*M)|_{U_i\times_XY}$ with pullback, along $U_i\times_XY\to U_i$, of $M|_{U_i}\cong B_{U_i}^{\oplus r_i}$. Step 5 makes this $B_{U_i\times_XY}^{\oplus r_i}$. This proves the lisse assertion, including varying finite ranks and rank zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O2-25231c1b9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 3 new nodes and every cited statement in full. Sources checked: native UpperStar.lean:80-312 (exists_opens_factor_of_eq_zero, exists_openImmersion_eq_comp_fst, isIso_upperStarAdicConstantSheafHom) and PullbackIsoOfLocallyGenerated.lean:50-95, 244-284; the split follows the native proof. The item had no proof on the base, so this is a first split, not a re-split. Item statement unchanged. I re-proved all 3 new nodes by hand. (1) Section presentation: shrink to an affine chart; the image K is compact in a finite-dimensional subspace, hence profinite; use Spec LC(K,R) and the clopen idempotents. (2) Zero relation: in an ultrametric field the balls are clopen and cut out by idempotents; localize at them; only continuity of t is needed. (3) Generators/relations criterion: using binary products, each colimit element is one class [t,phi]; (ii) gives local injectivity and (i) local surjectivity. None restates a clause of the item, and all are statement-only and self-contained. Edge cases checked: empty U, t=0, rank 0, varying ranks. Steps 1-5 are correct: in step 3, with c_g an isomorphism, the presheaf tensor is already g^{-1}M with transported action. Step 4 gets coefficient coherence from precomposition plus the adjunction. Fault (C1/C4), step 6: lem-pur-ringed-site-pullback-localization-universes takes abstract left adjoints of the module pushforwards, and the step asserted without citation that g^* and the slice pullbacks are those adjoints. FIX: cite lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction (on route via sk-thm-properbasechange; no cycle; no trf or pod node in its closure), add that the slice functor preserves finite limits and coverings and that left adjoints are unique, and update proof_deps. Batch-5: lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact (step 3) is generic topos exactness. Its closure has no trace-formula or Poincare theorem, only two trf definitions, and many other chapters cite it. It is genuinely outside both assumptions, so I accept it as a tool use, along with pur-ringed-site-localization and the fpqc base change leaf. Advisory: existing lem-sfb-totally-disconnected-coefficient-realization (f^{-1}C(|-|,D) = C(|-|,D) for totally disconnected D) gives a shorter alternative to step 2. Not a duplicate of any new node. No SGA. 1 fault.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
